findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no sanitizer solution prepared in the facility during food preparation or service. Education was conducted and a spray bottle was prepared measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no available stem thermometer for confirming proper cook temperature for TCS foods. Education was conducted an a stem thermometer was acquired. Ensure thermometers are available at all times of food prep and service.
findings.citation_text: 4-203.11 Temperature Measuring Devices, Food. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Celsius or dually scaled in Celsius and Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±1°C in the intended range of use. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed cheese sauce to temp at an improper hot holding temperature. The cheese sauce was tempted at 94F (probed). It appears that the cheese dispenser isn’t functioning properly and was discarded by PIC. The cheese sauce bag was also discarded. There was a backup sauce dispenser (and cheese bag) that is going to replace the broken one. The new cheese bag was probed at 137F. Be sure  that cheese sauce is held at 135F or above to ensure proper hot holding temperatures. 

The cheese sauce was probed at 94F. Discussed with PIC and cheese sauce was discarded. The cheesedispenser wasn’t functioning properly.

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on the top of storage bins, the ledge at serving window, the cabinets where there shop vac is stored. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) and (C)  (C)  Grease and soil accumulation present on the pot of the popcorn maker and the inside of the ice machine which is currently shut down and empty. Thoroughly clean all cooking equipment and pans. Reference 4-601.11(B) and (C). Clean before shutting down for the Winter and before open in the Spring. Cleaning frequency is not considered adequate to eliminate soil accumulation.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: Observed a metal utensil to be stored with the handle down inside of the food container. The food is pickle relish. Use proper utensil and do not leave utensil in the food overnight or while the facility is closed down for the winter. The relish was pulled in order for it to be discarded. 160(a) Food shall be prepared with the least possible manual contact, using suitable utensils and using surfaces that have been cleaned, rinsed, and sanitized to prevent cross-contamination.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: Observed single use plates to be packed up in soiled tubs for the winter break. Properly protect and store single use items at all times. Clean tubs. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Observed a bottle of oil stored in a cardboard box. The cardboard box was observed collecting oil. Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non-absorbant and easily cleanable. Cease to use cardboard to store oil this is a poor practice that can attract pests.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) (1) Observed the kettle in the popcorn machine to be soiled with food debris and an accumulation of grease. Food contact surfaces shall be cleaned and sanitized to prevent potential contamination of food. (2) Observed the drop guard on the ice machine to be soiled with an accumulation of what appears to be mold (black substance).

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Hotdogs in a ziploc bag used by the girls softball team and located in the concession stand fridge had a date mark of 4/4/16. Hotdogs should have been used or discarded by 4/10/16. Hotdogs were discarded in the trash.
 
Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and consumed, sold, or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
NOTE: Frozen foods do not fall under the same 7 day time frame for use. If products come in frozen, try to partially thaw just enough so the product may be broken apart (i.e. hotdogs) and leave the portion in the freezer that won't be used. Label what is needed and held in the refrigerator with the date the product is opened. If foods come in refrigerated, portions can be frozen to reduce the amount of product that requires discard after the 7 days are up. Once opened, make sure the dates are marked accordingly on products to reflect the proper use by time frame once pulled from the freezer and thawed for use. (i.e. frozen the same day opened (day 1); product must be used or discarded w/in 6 days after being placed in refrigeration/thawed for use).

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Soap was not available at the dispenser upon arrival of inspector. Manager stated the custodial staff will have to bring another bag of soap for the dispenser from storage. In the meantime, a bottle of dish soap was placed by the designated handsink.

Maintain a supply of soap and paper towels at handsinks to allow for proper handwashing at all times.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.280 - Popcorn scoop was observed on top of the popcorn machine. Top of the machine was soiled with general buildup. Scoop was placed inside the popcorn with the handle extended up out of product. 

Keep the scoop in the machine with the handle extended up out of the popcorn or provide a cleanable food grade container for storage between uses.
The importance of keeping the handle up out of popcorn was discussed (potential for cross contamination from microbes, specifically viruses, on hands).

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Players working the concession stand re-entered and did not wash hands prior to returning to tasks. One worker immediately prepared a bag of popcorn for a customer.
Handwashing upon entering the concession stand, between tasks, and after handling money were discussed. 
Educational handouts on when to wash hands, proper use of single use gloves, and proper handwashing technique (Section 750.510 of IL Food Code) provided.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food, clean equipment, or unwrapped single service articles.
Wash hands prior to putting on gloves and between glove changes. Gloves are meant for one task. Discard gloves when they become soiled, torn or there is an interruption in task..

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.150 - Internal temperatures of hamburgers in warmer were observed at 125F-132F. Hamburgers were grilled and wrapped to be placed in the warmer approximately one half hour prior to inspection. Concession stand worker noted the burgers are cooked to 160F prior to being pulled from the grill to be wrapped and placed in the warmer. The temperature dial of the warmer was turned to a higher setting. When the temperature was checked a little later one burger was up to 134F. All burgers must be sold or discarded by 5p.
Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135F/above when in hot holding. Store hot foods at 135F/above.
**Make sure the warmer is turned on to heat up prior to placing foods inside for hot holding**

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.280 & 290 - A) Scoop for popcorn was observed on a cloth towel. Store the scoop on a cleanable surface or in a clean container.
B) Scoops for coffee and coco were observed with handles down touching powders. Store scoops with handles extended up out of products.
C) Ice scoop holder was observed to be soiled in the bottom. Clean and sanitize the ice scoop holder as needed and maintain it clean to protect ice scoop and ice from potential contamination.
Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.
Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled with buildup:
A) inside grill lid (carbon buildup); and
B) cheese dispenser nozzle.
Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.
**Clean and sanitize the grill surface after use. Make sure surfaces inside popcorn machine are getting cleaned and sanitized as needed to minimize buildup of oil/food debris**

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - Storage area for plastic nacho containers was soiled with windblown dust and debris. Clean the storage area for plastic nacho containers as needed and maintain it clean.
Single-service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that will protect items from potential contamination. Maintain storage areas clean.
